name: Curiosity gap

pinned_evidence.title: The psychology of curiosity: A review and reinterpretation
States of curiosity modulate hippocampus-dependent learning
pinned_evidence.reason: neural — curiosity engages reward/memory circuitry (Gruber et al.)

evidence.basis: Curiosity arises from an information gap between what one knows and wants to know; the gap creates a drive to close it (Loewenstein 1994, information-gap theory). Neuroscience links curiosity states to reward and memory circuitry (Gruber, Kang et al.).
evidence.effect_size_note: The gap effect is well-established for attention and information-seeking; strength depends on the gap being neither trivial (already known) nor overwhelming (hopeless). Works on cold traffic, unlike most core mechanisms.

mechanism_summary_for_context: A gap between what someone knows and what they want to know creates a pull to close it. Surface a specific, resolvable unknown ('see your result', 'what your data reveals', an unfinished reveal) and the user is drawn to complete it. Unique in the set: works at the top of the funnel on cold traffic. The gap must resolve into real value — an unmet curiosity gap is clickbait and backfires.

preconditions.reason: requires a specific unknown the product can genuinely resolve; not applicable where there is no real reveal to deliver

applicability.culture_note: Curiosity is universal; what reads as an intriguing gap vs a trivial or manipulative one is an L3 surface parameter

implementations.generation_directive: Pose a specific, personally-relevant question framed around the user's own input, promising a personalized result rather than a generic one. The reveal must deliver genuine, specific value — a real personalized result, not a generic payoff. The gap should be resolvable within the flow, not endlessly deferred.

Open a specific loop and resolve it with real information, surfacing a single genuine standout finding rather than a vague summary. Reveal enough to make the gap felt, deliver the resolution as genuine value. Never tease a payoff the product cannot deliver.
copy_formulas: One thing stood out in your {data}

hard_rules.rule: The curiosity gap must resolve into genuine, specific value; teasing a reveal the product does not deliver (clickbait) is forbidden
The teased question must honestly represent what will be revealed; misleading curiosity hooks are forbidden

constraints.boundary_test: Does closing the gap give the user something genuinely worth their attention — or is it a bait that disappoints?

relations.note: Curiosity gap and variable reward co-occur (not knowing what the reward is), but differ: information gap vs reward unpredictability
An open question is a kind of open loop; distinct — CG-05 is an information gap, ZE-07 is task incompleteness

reference_examples.what: 'What your coffee order says about you' — canonical curiosity gap driving cold-traffic engagement; also the canonical clickbait cautionary case
'See your year in music' opens a personally-relevant gap resolved with genuine personal data
'See your idea's score' opens a resolvable gap the product genuinely answers with the evaluation
